problem: VLN agents use a late-fusion architecture in which unimodal representations (instruction, history, observation) are never aligned before the fusion module, leaving modality gaps. Prior alignment work (OAAM, RelGraph, FGR2R, DDL) only acts inside or after fusion, and needs annotations or post-fusion supervision.
motivation: Pre-fusion alignment helps vision-language tasks, but it is unexplored in VLN. Training signals for it are scarce, and VLN is sequential: history summarizes the whole trajectory while the observation at each step matches only a few landmarks, so a single alignment level would not fit both.
key_idea: Add self-supervised cross-modal contrastive losses before fusion at two levels: instruction-history (global and local) and landmark-observation (local), using a dual-level instruction built by appending extracted landmark nouns to the instruction.
insight: Aligning each visual modality with the text part it semantically corresponds to works better than aligning all vision with the whole instruction. The single-level ablation gives SPL 61.78 versus 63.39 for dual-level. Both levels contribute, and each instruction-history sub-alignment matters. Removing word-trajectory alignment lengthens trajectories (TL 14.58) and removing instruction-viewpoint alignment lowers SR most (71.56). Letting landmark words attend to instruction words through a shared encoder beats fully separated encoding.
method: Dual-level instruction: extract nouns with a POS-fine-tuned BERT as landmark words and append them to the instruction. A shared text encoder yields the [CLS], instruction word matrix X and landmark matrix L.

Instruction-history alignment: four similarities between global (CLS, mean-pooled trajectory) and local (words, history viewpoints) representations: IT, WT, IV, WV. Their scores are averaged into a contrastive InfoNCE loss L_IH over in-batch pairs.

Landmark-observation alignment: at each step t, compute a similarity matrix between the k view embeddings and the n landmark tokens. Apply a contrastive loss over local representations only, averaged over T steps (L_LO).
Attention-based reduce function R (from X-CLIP): a double softmax-weighted aggregation over rows and columns reduces similarity vectors or matrices to scalars.
Training: total loss = λ1·RL + λ2·IL + λ3·L_IH + λ4·L_LO, with λ3=0.01, λ4=0.1, τ=1, and a memory bank of 480 negatives. The framework is model-agnostic and is plugged into HAMT and DUET.

setting.backbone: HAMT and DUET (trained, with DELAN losses); BERT text encoder; CLIP-ViT-B/16 vision encoder for DUET
setting.training_data: Standard benchmark training data (R2R, RxR, R4R, CVDN) with the baselines' schedules; no extra data. Contrastive losses use in-batch negatives plus a memory bank.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (k views with relative angles) plus history of past observations and actions

numbers.extra: greedy single-run inference; baseline is authors' re-implementation

numbers.evidence: Table 4, goal progress on CVDN, DUET+DELAN Test-Unseen

numbers_note: Only the main DUET+DELAN and HAMT+DELAN variants are listed for each benchmark. Ablation numbers on R2R val-unseen are omitted.
results: DELAN improves both HAMT and DUET on R2R, RxR, R4R and CVDN. On R2R test-unseen, DUET+DELAN reaches SPL 62.69 versus 60.99 for the re-implemented DUET*. On R4R it gives HAMT +3.3 CLS and +3.7 nDTW. On CVDN test it adds 0.27 m (HAMT) and 0.23 m (DUET) of goal progress. Gains are consistent but mostly small.
limitations: Gains are modest on several splits (e.g. R2R val-unseen SR +0.55 for DUET, HAMT test-unseen SR +0.2) and come from single runs without variance.
Landmarks are extracted only as nouns with a POS tagger, and the method needs extra memory-bank negatives and hyperparameter tuning (λ3, λ4).
Evaluated only in simulated discrete-graph settings on top of two baselines (HAMT, DUET), not tested in continuous environments or on real robots.
